Context for coding agents working in this repository. The game is in `system/`; its own rules are in `system/AGENTS.md`.

## L1 System

| module | kind | purpose | depends on | used by | critical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `system/architecture` | tests | Architecture rules (ESLint): the boundaries between the simulation, the renderer and the browser. | - | - | no |
| `system/bugs` | tests | The planted bugs: bugs/manifest.json and one paired failing test per entry under bugs/tests/ (ADR-005). | sim | sim | no |
| `system/game/content` | content | Rooms as text maps, one file per room, and the tile order of the atlas. | - | render, asset-kit | no |
| `system/game/render` | ui | PixiJS rendering, keyboard, sound and the HUD. Reads WorldState and never writes it. | content, sim | asset-kit, trace-tool | no |
| `system/game/sim` | core | The pure deterministic simulation: movement, physics, the creature, input mapping. tick(state, input) is the only writer of WorldState. | bug-quest | bug-quest, render, asset-kit, trace-tool | **yes** |
| `system/tools/asset-kit` | tool | Turns raw art and audio in assets/ into public/assets/ with a manifest and provenance. | content, render, sim | - | no |
| `system/tools/trace` | tool | The trace tool: paints collision over a room painting and saves the text map. | render, sim | - | no |

## L2 Code

Architecture rules (`system/architecture/rules.js`; they break the build and cannot be bypassed in a change):

- `sim_does_not_import_render`: game/sim is the pure simulation and never imports the renderer or PixiJS, see docs/plan/02-design/simulation-architecture.md
- `sim_has_no_browser`: game/sim runs in Node, in a test and in a replay: no window, document, localStorage or fetch, see docs/plan/02-design/simulation-architecture.md
- `game_does_not_log`: game/ reports through WorldState.events and the waterfall of logs, not console; a console line is noise a visitor never sees, see AGENTS.md

Conventions (`system/AGENTS.md`):

- Every change to `game/sim/` ships a replay test in `tests/sim/`.
- Add content by adding a file or directory. Do not build central registries.
- Assets go through `pnpm assets`; the build fails on files that skip it and on outputs nothing consumes.
- Fixing a planted bug is one PR: correct the module the manifest names, remove the manifest entry, and the paired test passes. Never edit a paired test to make it pass; reviewers reject that.
- The main suite (`pnpm test`) never asserts planted behaviour. Only the paired test under `bugs/tests/` knows what the bug does.
- Never add code that detects developer tools or reads window size to change game behaviour.
- `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm bugs:check` must pass before a PR, judged by exit code.
- `window.wizard` on the page exposes `start`, `reset`, `paused`, `step(n, input)` and `state()` for automation. Use it in browser tests; do not remove it.
- One source for each fact: tile order, prop sizes, crystal positions and art rows live in one module or in the asset manifest, never in two places.
- Commit messages describe intent in plain sentences; PRs carry the preview URL.

## How to work

1. Change only the module named in the task. If another one must be touched, say why in the description.
2. Read the decisions and incidents linked in the task before you start.
3. Add a test for every behavior change; every change to `game/sim/` ships a replay test in `system/tests/sim/`.
4. Run the gate with `run_build` (`pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm bugs:check` in `system/`) and fix everything that is red.
5. Do not change `system/architecture/`, `system/bugs/tests/`, `sdlc/` or `scenarios/` to make the build pass.
